title: SDK playground: daynotes & doc fixes
body:
Daily scratchpad (devx SDK focus) - quick stream of consciousness

Date: 2026-03-10
Mood: caffeinated, urgent-ish

Top goals for today
- finish sample-app flow for streaming responses (node + python) and add to quickstart
- triage doc gaps flagged in #sdk-docs-review thread (esp. function-calling examples)
- prototype a minimal desktop Electron demo for local dev of Redwood Private

Open questions / constraints
- streaming example: should we show both SSE and websocket? currently examples only show SSE. Some users asked for WS.
- auth note: private deployment example needs KMS/HSM pointers — add short paragraph and link to security page.
- default retry/backoff recommendations aren't in the SDK readme (only in platform guide). move summarized guidance into sdk/README.

Scratch notes (copy-paste bits)
- Node streaming minimal (pseudo):
  const res = await client.stream({ model: 'rw-small', input: 'hello' })
  for await (const chunk of res) { process.stdout.write(chunk.text) }
  // show both streaming chunks and final object merge

- Python async streaming: use async for token in resp: yield token.text
- Add explicit example for handling function_call chunked outputs (user saw broken JSON across chunks)

Checklist (short items)
[ ] add SSE + WS streaming snippets to quickstart
[ ] write small section: handling partial JSON (function calling) with reassembly buffer example
[ ] add note about token accounting for streaming vs non-streaming endpoints
[ ] update error handling: map 429 -> exponential backoff example code
[ ] link to dedicated capacity docs from SDK readme when using reserved endpoints
[ ] create sample-app branch: sdk/stream-sample-app (start local server + browser)

Notes on sample app UX
- objective: show a tiny chat UI + streaming tokens + function call demo (call to mock weather API)
- tech: next.js for web, express for proxy, docker + env var for REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_BASE_URL (allow local dev against Private)
- include script: ./dev.sh -> sets env, runs docker compose (redis cache optional). keep it minimal (no infra required).

User feedback threads to incorporate
- Slack #sdk-docs-review: Elena flagged that the code samples use await client.generate(...) but some users prefer client.chat for multi-turn. Add clarifying paragraph and migration tip.
- GH issue #393: embeddings example uses old api version, update to new embed signature and add batch example.

Small PR plan (atomic changes)
1) docs: quickstart/streaming.md (SSE + WS + error handling) - small PR, reference: PR 412
2) sample-app: new folder /examples/streaming-chat - include README with local run instructions; add devx CI job to run linter only
3) sdk-readme: short auth/naming section + link to dedicated capacity SLA page

Local repro steps (notes for debugging)
- reproduce function-calling partial json bug: run streaming sample against rw-function-test model with long function schema; intentionally slow network (tc qdisc) to see chunk boundaries
- logs: instrument client to log chunk indices + cumulative buffer size, print reconstructed JSON parse errors

Pieces to copy into final PR description
- "This PR adds streaming websocket and SSE examples to the SDK quickstart and demonstrates safe reassembly of chunked function_call outputs. Also updates the embeddings example to the v2 signature and documents recommended retry/backoff behavior for 429 responses."

Personal TODO (not for PR)
- schedule 30m sync with Platform Docs (Ravi) to agree on where SLA and dedicated capacity links should live in SDK docs
- record a 5-min screencast showing local running of the sample app (for README)

Random ideas / future
- consider tiny interactive workshop slide deck (5 slides) for onboarding new hires to how to integrate Redwood SDK into an app in 10 minutes
- notebook-style tutorial (observable + python) that lets you toggle quantization/profile choices and shows token cost delta — maybe heavy but good for Optimize team collab

End-of-day quick log (write later): what shipped, blockers still open, PRs linked

-- Jamie
